newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Oct 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Oct 31.

text.p: The following is a summary of major South Korean political stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul.
Reuters has not checked the stories and does not gaurantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.
- Seventeen owners of bus companies in Seoul embezzled 23.8 billion won, give bribes to Seoul city government officials for favors in allocating lucrative bus operation lines.

- U.N. economic and social commission of Asia and Pacific adopts resolution to help reconstruct severed section of inter-Korean railways so it can ultimately be part of the projected trans-Asian railway.
- South Korea demands North Korea's disarmament efforts to help ease food shortage. Seoul said it will discontinue rice aid if Pyongyang snubs the demand.
- Korea's trade deficit with advanced countries hit $30 billion in the first nine months of this year, said the Bank of Korea.

- North Korea and Britain made secret contacts through a third country to discuss London's investments commitment for North Korea's Rajin-Sonbong free economic and trade zone, food aid, improvement of relations.
- The U.N. general assembly adopted a resolution urging North Korea and Iraq to comply with the nuclear safegaurds agreement.
- Korea's current account deficit widened to $1.4 billion in September from $453 million a year earlier. It exceeded $17 billion for January-September.
